# Summary of Studienstiftung
The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes, originally founded in Dresden in 1925 and re-established in Cologne in 1948, offers scholarships for undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students primarily in Germany. Eligibility includes full-time university students studying at institutions in Germany, other EU countries, or Switzerland, with no citizenship or age restrictions. Admission is through multiple nomination channels including schools, university professors, examination boards, competition winners, self-assessment tests, alumni, and arts nominations. Scholarships combine financial support—such as monthly allowances, insurance subsidies, tax-free payments, and additional child support—with academic support including summer schools, research groups, workshops, mentoring, and the organisation of conferences. Financial support is aligned with German Ministry of Education and Research guidelines and includes specific provisions for PhD candidates, who receive higher monthly awards.
The Studienstiftung also runs internal and open scholarship programs, collaborating with institutions like Saudi Arabia’s KAUST and the Beethoven House, and administers joint programs such as the McCloy Academic Scholarship. As of 2023, it approved over 2,400 scholarships annually, with a majority of scholars receiving standard allowances and a substantial share receiving additional need-based funding. The proportion of women among scholars was 55.4% in 2020. Leading German universities show high concentrations of Studienstiftung scholars, with institutions like Heidelberg University having over 2% of their student body sponsored. Notable alumni include multiple Nobel laureates and top scholars in natural and social sciences, business, politics, law, arts, and journalism. The organization is governed by a board with a history of distinguished presidents since its post-war re-founding.
